conceptual assets.information: The accumulated number of cycles held by the cycle counter is used for execution-time accounting and is returned through the CSR read path.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The counter state can be modified by CSR write data entering the low and high counter words at lines 135, 303, and 326. The debug and halt controls can suppress cycle increments through lines 108 and 131, making the returned count incorrect during normal operation.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write an unauthorized value to the cycle counter or assert a halt/debug control so that cycle measurements become false.

conceptual assets.information: The accumulated number of retired instructions held by the instruction-retirement counter is used for execution accounting and is returned through the CSR read path.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The counter state can be modified by CSR write data entering the low and high counter words at lines 154, 303, and 326. The debug and halt controls can suppress instruction-retirement increments through lines 110 and 150, making the returned count incorrect during normal operation.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write an unauthorized value to the instruction-retirement counter or assert a halt/debug control so that retired-instruction measurements become false.

conceptual assets.information: The indexed hardware performance-monitoring counter values record selected processor events and are used for performance and execution monitoring before being returned through the CSR read path.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Each performance counter accepts CSR write data through the instance connection at line 189 and the counter storage assignments at lines 303 and 326. The debug and halt controls suppress performance-counter increments through lines 112 and 185, allowing an integration-level control to produce incorrect measurements.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could overwrite a performance counter or assert a halt/debug control to falsify event-monitoring results.

conceptual assets.information: The stored per-counter event-selection configuration determines which processor events increment the hardware performance-monitoring counters and can be read back through the CSR interface.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: CSR writes change the stored event-selection configuration at lines 199 and 200, so an unauthorized write can alter which events are counted. The configuration gates use of the event inputs in the increment decision at line 112, so programming selections that match no event can disable the performance-monitoring function.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write zero or an unintended event mask so that performance counters report the wrong events or stop collecting measurements.

considered, not kept.reason: The pacing-pulse rule makes the event, halt, debug, and internal increment-enable controls part of the counter updates rather than separate information pieces.
The access-command-fields rule makes address, read, and write selection part of the counter or configuration information being accessed, not separate assets.
The RTL does not implement a time-counter value; time_rd is assigned only constants at lines 140, 164, and 237, so there is no meaningful information requiring a security objective.
The clock and reset inputs are excluded by the clock/reset rule and only time or reset other state.
